scope: Internal saved-data model-development readout, no simulation or scientific-source changes. All 64 Oct12 cold rows and 60 Oct10/11 controls. No physical, grid, domain or far-field independence claim.

definitions.core: Largest completely occupied central-plane integer hex ball, ring census checked against explicit site membership; tip=max occupied central-plane hex radius; gap=tip-core in lattice-radius cells. Occupancy is not mass.
definitions.plateau: Elapsed time since each row enters exact tip, sampled at 0, .25, .5, .75 of shortest positive plateau; row absolute ages differ. Adjacent event state retained without interpolating occupancy.
definitions.absoluteAge: Common absolute physical times at .25, .5, .75 and 1 of shortest run; at-or-before and next completed event states retained.
definitions.numerical: Existing operational row checker rederives convergence, ledger, fill-CFL, symmetry, stopping and terminal agreement. No new solver run. Timestep qualification is configuration/observable specific; no grid/domain/far-field qualification.

derivation: Reuses stateMeasure and bracket from out/hil-two-day-design-2026-10-12/cold-triage.mjs. Ring arrays retained in selected states; selection schedule matches prior retained cold.mjs. Timestep groups use the same plateau and absolute-age algorithm across all compared steps, avoiding different windows.

producerParity.interpretation: Only the four Oct11/Oct12 roster/entry files changed across the retained producer interval; core, solver, scientific worker, observations and readout definitions are unchanged.

limits: Retrospective internal model-development analysis, not a phase gate or physical mechanism identification.
Representation and domain/far-field sensitivity unresolved; a one-cell contrast is not grid independence.
Only recorded discrete states are used; adjacent events are brackets, not continuous interpolation.
Equal tip/plateau age and equal absolute age are separate comparisons, with different geometry.
Source parity spans these fixed producers; scalar kinetic interventions retain their explicit facet-arm identities.
No new simulation, producer, codec, parameter, or tracked source changes.
